previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A man with end-stage renal disease, diabetes, hypertension, and congestive heart failure was admitted for worsening shortness of breath and fluid overload after missing a dialysis session. His symptoms included orthopnea, fatigue, leg swelling, and postprandial vomiting. Imaging showed bilateral pleural effusions and pulmonary congestion consistent with heart failure exacerbation. He underwent hemodialysis, which improved his respiratory status and volume overload. His nausea was evaluated with a CT scan, which showed no obstruction, and was attributed to GERD. He was discharged stable on room air with medication adjustments, including discontinuation of pioglitazone and insulin dose reduction, and instructions to initiate CPAP therapy for sleep apnea.

Discharge Instructions:
You were admitted for fevers, muscle aches, and chills after 
hemodialysis.  These symptoms were caused by the influenza 
virus.  It will take seven days for this virus to run its 
course.  In the meantime, you should take tylenol as needed for 
aches and pains.  You should wear a mask for seven days from 
symptom onset to prevent transmission to others.

We also did studies that showed your heart to be functioning 
poorly.  This condition is called cardiomyopathy or heart 
failure.  Given this condition, you should be careful to avoid 
excess salt in your diet and continue to weigh yourself daily.  
You should continue your Avapro and metoprolol to treat this 
condition.  We initiated some tests to look for treatable causes 
of your cardiomyopathy.  You should follow up with your PCP for 
further testing for this.

Please resume your regular dialysis tomorrow.

INDICATION:  Abdominal pain and fever, on hemodialysis.

the symphysis after the uneventful intravenous administration of 130 ml
Optiray 350  contrast material.  Multiplanar reformatted images were obtained
and reviewed.

CT ABDOMEN WITH CONTRAST AND RECONSTRUCTIONS:  Moderate-to-large bilateral
pleural effusions again present, right greater than left.  No pericardial
effusion.

No focal liver lesion is detected.  There is no intra- or extra-hepatic
biliary duct dilatation.  The portal vein, splenic vein, and SMV are patent.
Celiac axis, SMA and ___ are patent. The adrenal glands, spleen, and kidneys
appear within normal limits. There is no hydronephrosis.  The body and tail of
the pancreas is not visualized suggesting prior resection.  No retroperitoneal
or mesenteric lymphadenopathy is detected. No dilated loops of small bowel are
identified to suggest obstruction.  No free fluid or free air is present
within the abdomen.  Mild calcified atherosclerotic plaque is present within
the abdominal aorta and iliac branches without aneurysmal dilatation.  The
appendix is well visualized without surrounding inflammatory stranding with
tip terminating at the inferior border of the liver (series 2:  image 44).

CT PELVIS WITH CONTRAST AND RECONSTRUCTIONS:  Bladder is mildly distended
without focal lesion detected within.  The distal ureters appear unremarkable.
The rectum and sigmoid colon is collapsed without inflammatory stranding to
suggest colitis.  No inguinal or pelvic adenopathy per CT size criteria.
Prostatic enlargement.

OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:  No suspicious lytic or sclerotic lesions.

1.  Moderate-to-large bilateral pleural effusions, right greater than left.

FINDINGS:  A single frontal view of the lower chest/upper abdomen is provided.
A nasogastric tube courses below the diaphragm with its proximal side port

IMPRESSION:  Satisfactory position of NG tube.

unresponsive.
